abstract: Automated seizure detection from electroencephalography (EEG) is a key step toward closed-loop brain-computer interface (BCI) systems and clinical decision support. We present DualBranchEEG, a dual-branch network that fuses (i) a temporal branch--a three-block 1-D convolutional encoder, a two-layer bidirectional LSTM and an additive attention layer--operating on the raw z-scored waveform, with (ii) a spectral branch--an MLP on log-power spectral density (PSD) features from Welch's method. We evaluate three-class classification (normal, interictal, ictal) on the Bonn University EEG dataset (500 single-channel recordings, 173.61 Hz) using a single stratified 70/15/15 split (seed 42). We position this work as a transparent reference implementation and exploratory comparison, not as evidence of superiority. A CNN-BiLSTM baseline (728,387 parameters; last-time-step readout, no attention, no augmentation) attains 96.00% test accuracy (72/75) and a macro AUC-ROC of 0.9795; five-fold stratified cross-validation of this baseline gives 98.40 {+/-} 1.52% accuracy and 0.9952 {+/-} 0.0071 AUC-ROC. The full DualBranchEEG (823,556 parameters) attains the same 96.00% test accuracy, macro F1 of 0.9543 and macro AUC-ROC of 0.9952. In the ablation, CNN-only, BiLSTM-only and CNN+BiLSTM+attention variants each reach 94.67%, and the full model is one test recording better; with only 75 test recordings these differences lie within sampling uncertainty (95% Wilson interval for 96.00%: 88.9-98.6%). Band-power differences between all class pairs are significant in all five canonical EEG bands. Grad-CAM, t-SNE and attention visualisations are reported as qualitative diagnostics only. We document all known methodological limitations, including PSD standardisation fitted on all 500 recordings and Welch's default 50% segment overlap.
